title: Protocol for assessing phagocytosis activity in cultured primary murine microglia
protocol: Prepare 20 mL of HBSS-H in a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 10 mL of HBSS-H to a 15 mL conical tube.
Transfer the remaining HBSS-H to a petri dish for tissue dissection.
Keep both the conical tube and petri dish on ice.
Thaw 100 μL DNase at 4°C.
Thaw 500 μL of 2.5% trypsin at 4°C.
Decapitate the pup to separate the head from the body.
Spray the head of the pup with ethanol.
Grip the back (dorsal side) of the body tightly and pull the arms outward.
Flip the pup so that its stomach (ventral side) is facing up.
Quickly decapitate the pup using sharp scissors.
Separate the brain from the skull to prepare for brain dissection.
Gently remove the skin from the top of the skull by pulling it away from the eye sockets with forceps.
Cut open the skull along the midline, starting at the brainstem opening and continuing near the eye sockets.
Peel back both sides of the skull from the midline cut to expose the brain tissue.
Use a small scoop tool to remove the brain from the base of the skull.
Place the brain in a petri dish containing HBSS-H and keep it on ice.
Remove the meninges, cerebellum/brainstem, olfactory bulbs, and hypothalamus with forceps.
Carefully cut into the midline of the brain, avoiding cutting through completely, to peel back the cortex and reveal the hippocampus.
Flip the brain from the dorsal to ventral side to reveal the striatum.
Remove the striatum with forceps.
Cut along the corpus callosum and peel tissue to isolate the hippocampus.
Ensure all meninges are removed from the cortex before collecting it into a prepared 15 mL conical tube containing HBSS-H.
Using a dissecting scope, dissect out the hippocampus and striatum to isolate the cortex.
Keep the tissue/HBSS-H cold during dissection.
Use forceps gently roll the cortical layer up to expose the hippocampus with the ventral side of the brain exposed and the anterior of the brain at the top.
From where the two cuts meet at midline, roll back the ventral part of the cortex away from midline to expose the hippocampus.
Invert the brain (posterior of the brain to the top) and slide curved forceps under the hippocampus to find the lateral edge.
Disconnect the hippocampus on both lateral sides from the cortex underneath.
Separate the hippocampus from the tissue that is on the inferior edge.
Identify the striatal tissue (inferior to the hippocampus) and use the curved forceps to remove the striatum.
Be careful to only remove the superficial portion of the tissue as there is more cortex underneath the striatum.
Collect the cortical tissue pieces from the petri dish and place into a designated 15 mL conical tube containing 10 mL HBSS-H.
Note: Optionally, cut the collected tissues into small pieces with forceps or razor blades before placing them into the conical to aid the trypsinization process.
Repeat dissection and tissue collection for all pups, collecting all cortical tissue together in the same conical tube of HBSS-H.
Keep samples on ice during collection.
Collect tissues into a second separate conical with HBSS-H for an additional genotype.
Aspirate HBSS-H from the conical tube containing collected cortical tissue using a vacuum suction system.
Add 4 mL HBSS to the conical tube with the settled cortical tissue.
Add 500 μL of 2.5% trypsin to the conical tube and mix well by inverting.
Add 70 μL DNase to the conical tube and mix well by inverting.
Incubate cortices with trypsin, HBSS, and DNase at 37°C for 15 min.
Invert tube every 5 min during incubation.
Homogenize the tissue with P1000 and P200 pipettes after completing the incubation.
Filter the tissue to isolate single cells.
Plate isolated cells with warmed media in a T-75 flask.
Cover the flask with aluminum foil at DIV 10–14.
Shake cells at 230 rpm for 3–3.5 h.
Collect media containing microglia and plate cells to a 12-well plate.
Incubate plated cells in 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 15 min.
Invert every 5 min during the initial incubation.
Monitor closely after the final inversion, waiting for cortical tissue to settle.
Aspirate HBSS/Trypsin/DNase solution once tissue is settled.
Wash tissue twice with 10 mL HBSS by inverting each time.
Add 2 mL HBSS and 30 μL DNase to the conical tube containing cortical tissue.
Homogenize the tissue slowly pipetting up and down 10 times.
Homogenize the cortical tissue with a P200 pipette, slowly pipetting up and down 10 times.
Add 2 mL of 10% FBS/DMEM/PS media (warmed to 37°C) to a 50 mL conical tube.
Place a 70 μm cell strainer on top of the 50 mL conical tube.
Wet the strainer with 10% FBS/DMEM/PS media to minimize cell loss or cell death upon first contact with the strainer surface.
Transfer homogenized cortical tissue using a P200 pipette.
Centrifuge isolated cells/media in the conical tube for 4 min 30 s at 300 rcf.
Aspirate media from the conical tube being careful to avoid the cell pellet.
Resuspend isolated cells in 5 mL of 10% FBS/DMEM/PS media (warmed to 37°C).
To a T-75 flask, add 15 mL of 10% FBS/DMEM/PS media (warmed to 37°C).
Pipette resuspended isolated cells into the T-75 flask and media.
Place the T-75 flask with media/isolated cells into a 37°C cell culture incubator maintained at 5% CO2.
Aspirate the media after at least 24 h (DIV 1) and replace it with 20 mL of new 10% FBS/DMEM/PS warmed to 37°C.
Change the media again at DIV 4 or DIV 5 to remove any additional debris.
Incubate new media for about an hour at 37°C before replacing to avoid cold shock in the culture.
Check for culture attachment and health with a microscope during growth period.
Replace media each week after initial changes.
Prepare a 12-well plate for the assay.
Add one 18 mm glass coverslip to each well.
Add 600 μL of 1× poly-l-lysine (PLL) to each well.
Agitate the plate to ensure cover glass is completely submerged.
Incubate the PLL-coated plate at 37°C for at least 2 hours.
Agitate the plate every hour to ensure proper coating.
Aspirate the 1× PLL from the coated wells near the end of microglia shake-off.
Wash the coated wells with cell culture grade water twice.
Remove any remaining wash solution after each wash.
The plate is now ready for plating with cell/media suspension.
Cover T-75 flasks containing mixed glia culture in aluminum foil.
Place covered flasks on shaker and secure them with tape.
Shake the flasks at 230 rpm between 18°C–26°C for 3 to 3.5 hours.
Check the cultures under a microscope after 3 hours of shaking.
Decide whether additional shaking is needed based on cell condition.
Collect media containing microglia from the flasks with a pipette once shaking is complete.
Transfer collected cells into a 50 mL conical tube immediately after collection.
Shake-off microglia from the non-adherent floating cell layer to isolate them from primary mixed glial cultures.
Centrifuge collected cells/media for 4 min 30 s at 180 rcf.
Aspirate media from the conical tube without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in 10% FBS/DMEM/PS media (warmed to 37°C).
Count the number of cells collected using a hemocytometer or other similar method.
Add media to the conical such that 1 ml of cell/media resuspension can be added to each well in a 12-well plate.
Tilt the 12-well plate so that microglia are evenly distributed across the top of the coverslip in each well after adding the cell suspension.
Incubate cells for 24 h at 37°C prior to LPS treatment.
Warm 1% FBS/DMEM/PS at 37°C before adding to wells.
Aspirate the media from the 12-well plate, being careful not to disturb the seeded cells.
Wash the seeded cells with 1 mL of 1% FBS/DMEM/PS media (warmed to 37°C).
Aspirate the remaining media immediately prior to treating the cells.
Add 800 μL of LPS or dPBS treatment prepared in media based on experimental conditions.
Incubate treated cells at 37°C for the desired length of time (e.g., 6, 12, and/or 24 hours).
Prepare 10 μL per well of bead treatment solution by mixing latex bead stock in a 1:10 ratio with 1% FBS/DMEM/PS.
Add 8 μL of bead mixture directly to treatment media already in wells, tilting plate to distribute evenly within the well.
Incubate plates at 37°C for 2 hours.
Aspirate beads and media without disturbing cells or cover glass.
Rinse wells with 1 mL 1× dPBS.
Aspirate and repeat the rinse process for two total washes with 1× dPBS.
Aspirate 1× dPBS from wells and add 1 mL 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Incubate wells with 4% PFA for 10 minutes at 37°C to fix cells.
Wash wells twice with 1 mL 1× dPBS.
Aspirate 1× dPBS from wells and add 1 mL 1× dPBS to each well for storage.
Protect plates from light by wrapping them in aluminum foil.
Store plates at 4°C.
Aspirate 1× dPBS storage solution from wells without disturbing cells or the cover slip.
Incubate coverslips with blocking solution for 1 hour and 30 minutes at 18°C–26°C, covered to protect from light.
Remove each coverslip from its well using forceps.
Place the coverslip cell-side down into the “bubble” on the parafilm.
Cover the coverslips with the lid of the 12-well plate.
Incubate in the 1° ab solution for 8–18 h at 4°C, covered to protect from light.
Prepare a negative control by adding Rabbit IgG Isotype control (5 mg/mL) to blocking solution at a 1:5000 ratio.
Incubate the coverslips used as negative controls with the same method described in steps 52–55.
Add 1 mL of 1× PBS to wells to wash coverslips.
Incubate the wells for 5 minutes on a rocker, covered.
Aspirate the 1× PBS from the wells.
Repeat the washing step twice more for a total of three washes.
Prepare 70 μL of secondary antibody solution per coverslip/well by adding Cy™5 AffiniPure Donkey Anti-Rabbit IgG to blocking solution at a ratio of 1:500.
Place the prepared secondary antibody solution onto parafilm stretched over a 12-well plate in 60 μL bubbles for each coverslip.
Pick up the coverslips with forceps and place each cell-side down into the “bubble” on the parafilm.
Cover the plates with lids and incubate at 18°C–26°C, protected from light, for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Return the coverslips to the wells of a 12-well plate after incubation.
Wash each coverslip with 1 mL of 1× PBS per well and incubate for 5 minutes.
Repeat the washing step twice more for a total of three washes.
Remove each coverslip from the wells using forceps.
Mount the coverslips on microscope slides with 1–2 drops of Invitrogen™ ProLong™ Gold Antifade Mountant containing DAPI.
Allow the mounted slides to dry at 18°C–26°C for 1–2 hours, covered.
Coat the edges of each coverslip on the slide with a thin layer of clear nail polish.
Allow nail polish to dry at 18°C–26°C for 8–18 h, covered.
Store slides at 4°C for long-term storage.
Image microglia and beads using a microscope; a Zeiss Confocal microscope or a Zeiss fluorescence microscope with Apotome and a 20× lens.
Determine an exposure time for each channel to be used: DAPI, fluorescent beads, and microglia.
Maintain the same exposure time constant between imaging different slides in the experiment.
Determine the Z-stack number and Z-stack interval for imaging.
Recommend a Z-stack interval between 0.5–1 μm to differentiate beads easily.
Recommend 10–15 Z-stacks based on chosen interval.
Find an area of the coverslip that includes multiple cells.
Set up the first Z-position by focusing upwards using imaging software.
Set up the last Z-position by focusing downwards using imaging software.
Collect 2–3 Z-stack images per coverslip.
Optimize image parameters for all cells in the experiment.
Use optimized exposure time and Z-stack settings consistently across experiments.
Plate, treat, assay, and immunostain 2-3 coverslips per genotype, treatment, and length.
Image each coverslip following immunostaining.
Collect 2–3 images for quantification per coverslip.
Count beads per microglia using Fiji - ImageJ software.
Assess every microglia (Iba1/DAPI positive) for co-localization of beads in each Z-stack.
Average all beads per microglia values for each treatment and treatment length.
Statistically compare the averages between each genotype.
